doc: The input picture, resized to the working resolution that every mask downstream is traced at.
label: Image

doc: Letters as a mask, ready for a Stencil node (letters become cut-outs, and the Stencil bridges the islands inside letters like O, A and B). Several lines are centred. To put text on a picture, there is no overlay yet: use it as its own stencil or tile it next to the picture's plate.
label: Text

doc: Crops, flips and rotates the picture before tracing. The order is crop, flip, turn, then the fine rotation, which grows the canvas to fit and fills the corners white (no paint). Put it right after the Image node so every later node sees the corrected picture.
label: Crop & rotate

doc: Dark areas become paint (holes); invert to make light areas the holes.
label: Threshold

doc: Quantizes the picture to N colours (k-means in Lab space) so every region has exactly one flat colour.
label: Reduce colours

doc: Splits an image into one mask per flat colour, darkest first (colour 1), so each colour can feed its own Stencil. An image with more colours than the setting is reduced first. Every mask is true where that colour is (paint). Outputs beyond the number of colours are hidden.
label: Split colours

params.label: Drop specks smaller than (% of image)
params.name: min_area

doc: Ranks the colours of a reduced image by lightness. The darkest becomes solid paint, the lightest stays empty, and the tones between get patterns that thin out step by step. Dots leave islands that the stencil bridges. One tone per colour of the input (up to 10).
label: Apply tone patterns

doc: Rounds the pixel staircase of a mask. The mask is enlarged by the supersample factor, blurred by the smoothing radius (in source pixels) and cut at half strength, so edges become curves and sharp corners round off. Very thin strokes can vanish at large radii. Feed the result to a Stencil node: bridging still runs on it, so it stays island-free. The output is supersample-times larger in each direction, and the stencil grid grows with it.
label: Smooth mask

doc: Binary morphology on a mask (paint = true). Erode shrinks paint and dilate grows it; open drops specks and thin necks, close fills pinholes and gaps; gradient is the outline band; white-hat is what open removed, black-hat is what close added. Thin (Zhang-Suen) reduces strokes to one-pixel lines that stay connected, Skeleton is the morphological skeleton (3x3 square). Hit-or-miss marks pixels matching a 3x3 pattern: isolated pixels, endpoints, convex corners, junctions, or your own. The kernel (square, disc, diamond, cross, line at an angle, ring) applies to the erode-to-black-hat operations; paint at the picture edge is not eroded. The output is the mask of the affected pixels, so gradient, hats, skeleton and hit-or-miss give only those pixels.
label: Reshape paint

doc: Turns a mask into vector shapes: closed Bézier outlines with holes, smooth curves and sharp corners kept. Feed it to a Vector stencil, so the outlines need no pixel smoothing.
label: Trace

doc: Replaces sharp pointy corners of traced outlines with a small tangent arc, so tips are not too fragile to cut or print. Only paint tips are rounded by default (they lose material); empty spikes that poke into the paint are rounded too when asked (they gain material). The arc is shortened where the neighbouring edges are short, so a very sharp tip may keep a smaller radius. The second output shows the cut-off tips.
label: Round corners

params.label: Also round empty spikes poking into the paint
params.name: round_concave

doc: Cleans traced shapes by size. Specks are separate paint pieces and holes are unpainted regions enclosed by paint; each smaller than the area limit is removed, together with anything nested inside it. Filling a hole means that part is cut out too, so the stencil needs no bridge there. 'Keep only the N largest' drops the other separate paint shapes. The second output shows what was removed.
label: Remove islands

doc: Rasterises vector shapes back to a mask at any resolution, so curves can feed the raster nodes.
label: Rasterise shapes

doc: Turns a mask into a watertight, island-free 3D plate with bridges. Raised bridges keep the first layer true to the artwork: islands and all, with the paint filling underneath. Minimum first-layer width adds a tapered flare only at the bed; bridge selection still uses the original outline. Connect a Tile layout instead of a mask to build every tile as a stencil of its own (the Parts output): the width and margin then come from the layout, and a cut never creates an island.
label: Stencil

params.label: Longest bridge in spread mode (x shortest)
params.name: bridge_max_length

doc: Builds the plate directly from vector outlines with polygon booleans, bridges enclosed material islands, and extrudes the result. Mesh detail controls curve flattening accuracy. Raised bridges are built from vectors too, as stepped strips, so curves stay smooth. Minimum first-layer width adds a tapered flare only at the bed; bridge selection still uses the original outline. Connect a Tile layout instead of shapes to build every tile as a stencil of its own (the Parts output); the width and margin then come from the layout.
label: Vector stencil

params.label: Longest bridge in spread mode (x shortest)
params.name: bridge_max_length

doc: Divides the plate into tiles before it is built, on an even grid, and reserves a block of material for every connector pocket (at the spot along each seam that covers the least paint). Connect it to a Stencil (from a mask) or a Vector stencil (from shapes) in place of their mask or shapes: each tile is then a stencil of its own, bridged on its own, so cutting never creates an island. The plate width and margin are set here; the stencil node supplies thickness, bridges and the rest. The Parts output goes on to Pads and Screws like the Tiles node's. In the viewer, drag a seam or a connector block to adjust the layout by hand; edits are kept as offsets from the automatic layout and ignored if they stop fitting.
label: Tile layout

doc: Cuts the mesh density in two steps. Decimation then collapses vertices on flat faces and straight edges, as long as the surface moves less than the shift (creases stay, the mesh stays closed), within the layer interval too. Outline edges that several layers share are smoothed and simplified once, so layers keep sharing vertices; the shift stays within the tolerance and, with the material option, only adds material. No layer overhangs the one below by more than the angle. The layer height is the stencil's. Layers outside the interval keep their shape (an interval short of the whole plate saves few vertices). Run it right after a stencil, before post-processing.
label: Remesh

params.label: Decimate flat faces and straight edges
params.name: decimate

doc: Splits the plate into printable tiles on a seam grid, with glued connector rods in blind seam holes. Adds raised threaded pads and threaded or plain mounting holes in the frame, and joiner and extender plates that bridge the seams. Download everything as a ZIP.
label: Tiles & mounting (old)

params.label: Distance from a seam to the hole (mm)
params.name: mount_offset

params.label: Extender plate: distance between the two rows of holes (mm)
params.name: mount_extend

doc: Cuts the plate into tiles no larger than the given size, as evenly as it can, and joins them with glued connector rods in blind holes at the seams. Seam clearance removes the specified total width from each seam, evenly split between its two tiles; 0 keeps the current flush fit. Connector pockets and rods extend across the gap while keeping the configured pocket depth in each tile. A seam may move a few millimetres to cross more material, so the connectors have room. When a cut leaves a piece of a tile hanging free, bridges tie it to its tile, so no tile has islands.
label: Split volume

params.label: Seam bevel angle (deg from vertical, 0 = straight)
params.name: seam_angle_deg

params.label: Add material where no connector fits
params.name: reinforce

doc: Adds threaded pads for fixing the stencil to a frame, wall or board, and optional through-holes, to the tiles from a Tiles node. Set the pad thread to none for a plate without pads. Pads sit on the middle of the margin band at the corners and, on edges longer than the limit, evenly between them. Holes are spaced along the band. Unflipped mounting holes have centered, chamfered support bosses that rise from the plate; their height is set by Pad & mounting height, and their flared base stays within the margin and tile. The through-hole remains open. A spot that would fall on a seam or a connector slides along its edge until it is clear, so every pad and hole sits in one tile. Printed flipped, pads are plain threaded holes. Needs a margin of at least the pad diameter (thread + 4 mm). When there are mounting holes either side of a seam it also outputs the plates that screw the tiles together: joiner_<screw>.stl (two holes, on the two mounting holes either side of a seam) and extender_<screw>.stl (four holes, a second row the set reach further out), as thick as the pads are high, with the mounting holes' clearance and thread. Print one joiner per seam crossing.
label: Add pads & mounting holes

params.label: Pad & mounting height above the plate (mm)
params.name: pad_height

params.label: Add pads along edges longer than (mm)
params.name: long_edge

params.label: Joiner hole distance from a seam (mm)
params.name: joiner_offset

params.label: Extender plate: distance between the two rows of holes (mm)
params.name: extend

doc: Puts a border of blank slabs around the assembled plate, as thick as the plate. The border is as wide as set and is cut into slabs no longer than the longest slab, with a corner slab at each corner. Slabs are butt-jointed to the plate and to each other with joiner plates, screwed through holes that mirror the plate's own mounting holes (same screw as the Pads node): each joiner spans a seam, with one hole in each part. With more than one ring, each ring wraps the one inside it, and the screw holes that join it are added to that ring. The plate's holes along its outer edge are used by the joints, so they no longer fix it to a wall; turn on the wall holes to mount the outer ring instead. The gap (0 by default, up to 1 mm) is left between the slabs and between the slabs and the plate, to allow for printed parts coming out a little big: each slab gives up half of it on every side, the screw holes do not move. Print one joiner plate per joint (turn it for vertical seams), or the square one (four holes) where a stronger seam is wanted. The node also outputs the bolt and the nut to print, two of each per joiner plate (counts in the report): a hex-head bolt with a real thread, long enough to go through the joiner and the slab and reach a nut (or set a length), and a hex nut whose thread is a little looser than the bolt (nut clearance, radial; raise it if the nut will not turn on your printer, lower it if it is sloppy). Print the bolts head down and the nuts flat. When the plate's holes are threaded the bolt can also screw straight into the slab. Each slab is numbered by a pocket in its top face, as deep as set (one layer of the plate by default; the numbers follow the ring, inner ring first, corners first), clear of the screw holes; turn it off or resize it as needed. Needs a margin greater than zero and a mounting hole screw in the Pads node; the node says so if a slab would get no screw hole.
label: Expand margin

params.label: Add a bolt and a nut for the joiner plates
params.name: hardware

params.label: Mounting holes along the outer edge
params.name: wall_holes

doc: Looks at every tile of the parts and finds the solids that are not connected to each other, such as small pieces a seam cuts off or specks a bridge could not reach. Only the biggest ones, by volume, are kept: the number set by Fragments to keep per tile, 1 by default, and the others are removed. Tiles already within that number are left as they are, and connector rods and other files pass through unchanged. The report lists, for each tile cleaned, how many pieces and how much volume were removed, so you can see if something sizeable went. Every cleaned tile is checked watertight. Put it after Split volume (and before Add pads & mounting holes).
label: Remove fragments

doc: Packs the stencils of several colours (one per input, darkest first) into one ZIP. Every plate gets the same registration holes in its margin, so after the first colour is painted the pins or paint dots through the holes line up the next layer. Two holes sit on a diagonal and three form an L, so a layer cannot be laid on rotated. All plates need the same size: same picture, plate width and margin. The holes need a margin of at least the hole diameter plus 1 mm.
label: Colour set

params.label: Add alignment pins to the set
params.name: pins

doc: Printable hex-head bolt and hex nut with real threads (M3 to M10). The bolt tip narrows over the last thread pitch (set the taper and its length in pitches) so it finds the hole; the taper is 0 for a plain end. Connect a Add pads & mounting holes node and it also prints a joiner plate and an extender plate that bridge the seams over the frame, sized for that node's mounting screw. Also a joiner plate you size by hand: two holes of the screw size the given distance apart (centre to centre), as high as set, with the padding of material round the holes and rounded ends, plus a second plate with four holes (the second row the extender reach further out). The holes are plain clearance holes for the bolt, or real threads if Threaded holes is on, with the clearance set (0.4 mm diametral, like the mounting holes of the Pads node). Also a calibration strip of connector holes with growing clearance: try the rod in each and keep the snuggest.
label: Make screws, nuts & plates

params.label: Extender plate: distance between the two rows of holes (mm)
params.name: extend
